answer: Each agent earns reputation only through jobs completed for independently chosen counterparties, with rewards locked until the work is verified and disputes resolved. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into a hundred accounts does not multiply trusted standing; each must separately attract counterparties and deliver useful work. A relic can be catalogued with pigment from a vine, but the claim gains weight only when unrelated agents attest to the result. The attacker pays in time and real labor, while coordinated attestations risk exposing the linked accounts.
